title: Error running `podman system hyperv-prep` from Azure VM Run Command
body:
### Issue Description

I am trying to setup podman automatically in an azure VM I am provisioning in terraform. I am installing hyper-v and podman with terraform via [Azure VM Run Commands](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/windows/run-command?tabs=portal%2Cpowershellremove).

I try running the command both as SYSTEM and the `azureuser` user (who is local admin) both before and after logging in with RDP.  It fails between `These entries will persist even when all machines are removed.` and `Added user w-pdm-hpv-vm\azureuser to the Hyper-V Administrators group`. If I run the command from RDP as the `azureuser` user it succeeds, and further attempts to run it from an Azure VM Run Command succeeds.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create an azure VM
2. Install Podman via MSI via Run Command
3. Run `podman system hyperv-prep` in a run command

```
# -------------------------------
# VM Run Command - Prepare Podman Hyper-V Provider
# -------------------------------
resource "azurerm_virtual_machine_run_command" "prepare_podman_hyperv" {
  name               = "prepare-podman-hyperv"
  location           = azurerm_resource_group.rg.location
  virtual_machine_id = azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm.id
  depends_on         = [azurerm_virtual_machine_run_command.install_podman]
  run_as_user        = azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm.admin_username
  run_as_password    = azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm.admin_password

  parameter {
    name  = "VmAdminUser"
    value = azurerm_windows_virtual_machine.vm.admin_username
  }

  source {
    script = <<-EOT
      $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

      $podman = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Podman\podman.exe'

      if (-not (Test-Path -Path $podman)) {
          throw 'Podman executable not found.'
      }

      # Pre-create the HKLM VSock entries so the runner account can create
      # and manage Hyper-V machines without an elevated token.
      & $podman system hyperv-prep

      if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
          throw 'Podman Hyper-V preparation failed.'
      }
    EOT
  }
}
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

_No response_

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

Azure VM provisioned with terraform

### Additional information

Running `podman system hyperv-prep` once from RDP makes this go away.

comments.body: I'm guessing from reading `cmd/podman/system/hyperv_prep_windows.go` that the issue is in `go.podman.io/podman/v6/pkg/machine/hyperv` specifically `IsHyperVAdminsGroupMember()`
/assign i would like to work on this issue

I found the root cause and tested the branches on my fork against it on an Azure VM.
